body:
## Context

Found while verifying the 1.11.0 release-audit OpenCode blocker: the shared adapter core writes EVERY host's deny marker with contentHash:null (packages/context-handoff/lib/adapter.mjs:474-479 passes contentHash: null into ensureDenyMarker). The audit attributed the unresumable marker to the OpenCode adapter, but ticket_id was the only host-specific part — the null content_hash is universal, and bin/handoff.mjs's resume path refuses a null content_hash ("final content_hash is null — cannot resume"). Every band-deny marker minted by the in-band adapter path is therefore resume-refusing by construction, on all hosts, and only host repair can rebind it. Bind the real final/capture content hash (S2 capture store, lib/capture.mjs / lib/final.mjs) at marker-mint time when one exists, so the deny the adapter writes is the deny the recovery CLI can actually consume.

## Acceptance criteria

1. When a capture/final exists for the session, the minted deny marker carries its content hash (non-null). verify: `node --test packages/context-handoff/test/*.test.mjs` exits 0 with a marker-binding test present.
2. When none exists, the marker stays null-hash and the deny text says host repair is required (honest degrade). verify: same suite pins the degrade wording; exits 0.
3. Adapter drift tests across the four harness copies stay green. verify: `node --test packages/context-handoff/adapter-test/*.test.mjs` exits 0.

ADDITION (2026-08-22, from the #540 round-1 fix): also expose the deny-marker OWNER as a structured field on evaluateHandoffPreToolUse's result (today {deny, reasons, ensuredMarker, denyEverWritten} at adapter.mjs:632 — the owner exists only inside the D3:unauthorized_open:<owner> reason string pushed at mutation-gate.mjs:225). Host recovery tails currently string-parse that reason to name the repair/resume target; a structured owner removes the format coupling. Same shared-adapter surface as the contentHash fix, so it belongs in this ticket.
title: context-handoff adapter: ensureDenyMarker hardcodes contentHash:null for every host — bind the real final content hash
